raw_case_text:
A 36-year-old male, diagnosed with human retroviral disease and initiated on antiretroviral treatment (ART) for 3 months, presented with passage of frank blood per rectum of 2 months and a cough with expectoration of 3 weeks. He had also developed multiple oral and genital ulcers over the past 2 weeks. His CD4 count was 134 cells/mm3 at admission.
On examination, he had a BMI of 17.2 kg/m2. Pulse oximetry saturation of 88% confirmed hypoxia. There was generalized lymphadenopathy, multiple snail track ulcers in the oral cavity, and a solitary painless penile ulcer. The rest of the systemic examination was unremarkable. The patient had undergone a colonoscopy previously which detected an ulcero-proliferative lesion in the anal canal suspicious of malignancy. Laboratory investigations revealed severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, and negligible viral load with an elevated D-Dimer. Microbiological examination of the sputum was negative for bacteria and acid-fast bacilli. Persistent hypoxia prompted us to do a computed tomography chest with pulmonary angiogram that showed no evidence of pulmonary embolism. However, it revealed bilateral parenchymal nodules (peri-lymphatic) with central and peri-broncho vascular ground glass opacities, bilateral mild pleural effusion, and interlobular septal with fissural thickening, suggestive of lymphangitis carcinomatosis [Figure 1]. This clinical presentation compelled us to initiate treatment for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. Nonetheless, he failed to respond to the treatment and hypoxia persisted. A Treponema pallidum Hemagglutination test was done as a part of workup for the penile ulcer, which turned positive. He was diagnosed to have secondary syphilis and was started on benzathine penicillin for the same. At this point, a differential diagnosis of primary anorectal malignancy with lymphangitis carcinomatosis vs. pulmonary syphilis was considered. Meanwhile, the patient continued to have bleeding per rectum and therefore underwent a repeat colonoscopy which confirmed the persistence of an ulcer-proliferative lesion and a biopsy was taken. The patient's clinical condition rapidly deteriorated with worsening hypoxia and he succumbed to massive hemoptysis on the third day of his illness. The biopsy report revealed a spindle cell proliferation in the lamina propria with the spindle cells showing mild atypia, suggesting KS [Figures 2 and 3]. This was further confirmed by a positive CD34 staining of the biopsy specimen which subsequently confirmed the diagnosis of KS [Figure 4].

subjective.chief_complaint: A 36-year-old HIV-positive male presented with a 2-month history of frank hematochezia, a 3-week history of productive cough, and a 2-week history of multiple oral and genital ulcers.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with 2 months of bright red blood per rectum (previously evaluated by an outside colonoscopy showing an ulceroproliferative anal canal lesion suspicious for malignancy), followed by 3 weeks of cough with expectoration and 2 weeks of multiple oral and penile ulcers.
subjective.past_medical_history: Diagnosed with HIV infection 3 months prior to admission and initiated on antiretroviral therapy (ART).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for hematochezia, productive cough, dyspnea/hypoxia, oral ulcers, and a painless penile ulcer. Home medications: antiretroviral therapy for 3 months.

objective.physical_examination: BMI was 17.2 kg/m2 and room-air pulse oximetry saturation was 88% (hypoxic). Physical examination revealed generalized lymphadenopathy, multiple oral mucosal 'snail-track' ulcers, and a solitary painless penile ulcer, with an otherwise unremarkable systemic examination.
objective.routine_investigations: Laboratory studies showed severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, elevated D-dimer, and a negligible HIV viral load. Sputum Gram stain, bacterial culture, and acid-fast bacilli smears were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Admission CD4 count was 134 cells/mm3. CT pulmonary angiography ruled out pulmonary embolism but demonstrated bilateral perilymphatic parenchymal nodules, central and peribronchovascular ground-glass opacities, mild bilateral pleural effusions, and interlobular septal and fissural thickening resembling lymphangitis carcinomatosis. Repeat colonoscopy with biopsy of the persistent ulceroproliferative anal canal lesion revealed lamina propria proliferation of mildly atypical spindle cells positive for CD34 on immunohistochemistry, confirming Kaposi sarcoma.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed secondary syphilis co-existing with advanced AIDS-associated anorectal and pulmonary Kaposi sarcoma (initially mimicking Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and lymphangitis carcinomatosis/pulmonary syphilis), established via positive serum TPHA alongside oral snail-track ulcers and penile chancre, and CD34-positive anorectal Kaposi sarcoma histopathology. Treated empirically for PJP and initiated on intramuscular benzathine penicillin for secondary syphilis, but his hypoxia rapidly worsened and he died of massive hemoptysis on hospital day 3.
